mappings.review_reason: No endpoint was supplied; retain the missing state rather than infer a measurement from heterogeneous support text.
The sole row contains only ellipses in its endpoint, measurement, unit, skin source, and support; keep it as an explicit extraction placeholder.
The row is an estimated daily dermal intake rather than an experimental absorption or permeation measurement, so it remains a separate estimate concept.
This is an integrated amount collected or penetrated through a specified time and must remain distinct from instantaneous or steady-state flux.
The single row reports formulation-dependent material remaining on the skin surface; its ambiguous source label is preserved instead of merging it with absorbed or permeated amount.
Direct dermal or percutaneous absorption endpoint; measurement unit, reference basis, study design, and species retain amount-versus-fraction and local-versus-systemic distinctions.
These rows are dermal open-flow microperfusion AUC and Cmax measurements; keep their local dermal pharmacokinetic scope distinct from the broader skin-exposure inventory.
Space-separated spelling of the same administered dermal dose endpoint.
Applied dose is an exposure input and remains separate from the amount absorbed, retained, or permeated.
Physical diffusivity D in area per time; preserve it separately from permeability coefficients and partition parameters.
The support explicitly calls the values diffusivity and reports area-per-time units; this is an extraction-schema alias of diffusion coefficient.
The source explicitly names a fitted distribution coefficient; retain it separately because the support does not establish equivalence to diffusivity or a dimensionless partition coefficient.
Mass or mole transport rate per area and time; distinct from cumulative amount, permeability coefficient, and maximum-flux-only endpoints.
Reviewed truncation of flux; the supporting row explicitly describes patch flux.
Absolute time before measurable or steady permeation; keep separate from time-to-peak and comparator-relative lag time.
These three rows report lag time as percent of an unprotected control, so they cannot share the absolute lag-time concept.
Explicit maximum flux Jmax is retained separately from generic or steady-state flux.
Support identifies Kp as a compartmental dermatokinetic rate constant with inverse-time units, not a length-per-time permeability coefficient.
Support and area-per-time units explicitly identify these values as diffusion constants or effective diffusion coefficients despite the raw endpoint label.
The fitted D/L2 absorption parameter has inverse-time units and is not interchangeable with D or Kp.
The source reports log Kp; preserve the transformed quantity rather than mix it with linear permeability coefficients.
Linear or explicitly transformed skin permeability coefficient; canonical units and transforms retain its measurement axis.
Water-vapor transmission or TEWL-model rate in mass per area per time is physically distinct from solute permeability coefficient.
Permeation flux is an exact lexical specialization of flux and the rows use the same mass-per-area-per-time measurement.
Narrative presence or absence of absorption without a transferable scalar remains distinct from quantitative dermal absorption.
Predominantly narrative penetration evidence; any extracted depth or time remains separated by canonical unit and reference semantics.
The source asserts a quantitative-penetration endpoint but its sole value is compartment-localized prose; preserve the label without merging or fabricating a scalar.
The sole row is a missing enhancement-ratio reference mislabeled as radiation level; retain it as a distinct auditable source artifact.
Absolute difference or increase in transport rate versus a comparator; preserve it separately from absolute flux and unitless relative penetration.
Signed comparator difference in lag time; distinct from absolute lag time and relative ratios.
Fitted K-prime partition-length parameter in centimeters; preserve this model parameter independently of flux and permeability.
Physical penetration depth in skin or a skin model, not an absorbed amount, transport rate, or relative ratio.
Comparator difference in time to peak penetration or flux; keep separate from lag time and penetration depth.
Signed difference in Ktrans between conditions, not an absolute permeability coefficient.
Unitless, fold, percent-change, or narrative comparison of penetration; reference scope and basis retain the comparator semantics.
Skin absorption is a direct lexical synonym of dermal absorption; canonical unit, reference basis, design, and species continue to separate measurement strata.
Broad measured or estimated local skin exposure inventory; retain it apart from the specific dermal microperfusion PK endpoint.
Reviewed truncation of skin_exposure_measurement in otherwise ordinary dermal-exposure rows.
Amount or fraction entering skin in a named penetration experiment; kept distinct from systemic absorption, through-skin cumulative permeation, and qualitative penetration.
Amount retained or deposited within a skin compartment; distinct from through-skin permeation and tape-strip-specific stratum-corneum recovery.
Reviewed pluralization typo of skin_retention.

mappings.endpoint_name: skipping further identical pattern for brevity; full extraction would include all conditions and compartments
mappings.review_reason: This is an extraction-process message rather than a biological endpoint; retain it as an explicit artifact rather than infer skin distribution.
The single row contains narrative skin deposition but no statistical measurement; preserve the source label as a non-endpoint audit artifact.
Tape-strip recovery is specific to sequential stratum-corneum sampling and remains distinct from whole-skin retention or penetration.
Steady-state dermal tissue-to-plasma distribution ratio; preserve its denominator and PK meaning separately from local concentration or retention.
Transdermal flux is the same transport-rate concept as flux; calculated-estimate study design keeps these seven in-silico Jm values from experimental strata.
